items.title: Lisa Parrott interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, June 22, 2021
items.q: through a friend of mine Kenny Wessel, guitarist who played with him for quite a few years.

ctx.x: I’ve been reading, I wish I was more familiar with Ornette and his concepts but I’ve been reading about it. But much of it makes me scratch my head I must admit. And so I’m going to take the opportunity to ask you to sort of explain some of it.

Well Ornette too, from what I’ve read, I did meet him a couple of times. I went to one of his birthday parties, that was amazing. That’s from — I have a lot of stories — through a friend of mine Kenny Wessel, guitarist who played with him for quite a few years. But it seems like Ornette every time you asked him, “What is harmolodics?” he would answer a different way. And me and my friends in Sydney came up with a way of what we thought or what I thought harmolodics was. And for me it was just a very basic concept…

been into the logic of melody, how if you — it’s almost like if you do it, think of it in terms of a philosophy, if you have a statement here for the music to run its true course it has to go here and it has to go here and it has to go here. So following the natural logic of melody of one instrument and then layering that with another instrument like that makes up the harmony because there’s no pre-set form.
